old_title: Rangers and Celtic clash in Scottish League Cup quarter-finals with away fans banned
new_title: Impressive Rangers thrash Old Firm rivals Celtic in League Cup quarter-final
old_text:
Rangers host Celtic in the Scottish League Cup quarter-finals and the first meeting of the Old Firm this season. But there will be no away fans at Ibrox following the shocking scenes that followed last season's Scottish Cup quarter-final between the teams.
There is a change in the dugout this season with Derek McInnes taking charge of Rangers, after he led Hearts to the brink of the title only to be denied by Celtic at the end of last term.
McInnes has steadied the ship at Rangers after a difficult start, while Martin O'Neill's team have started the campaign with seven consecutive wins domestically, although both sides have made an absolute mess of Europe.
Celtic were denied the League Cup following a shock defeat to St Mirren in last year's final but they went on to win both the Premiership and the Scottish Cup.
Follow live updates from Rangers v Celtic, below
Celtic team news
Here's how Celtic will line up today.
A bit of a surprise in that the impressive Haissem Hassan has been dropped, with Sebastian Tounekti preferred. Tounekti isn't necessarily universally popular with Celtic fans...
Tounekti is likely to play on the left, with Camilo Duran on the right and record signing Kasper Hogh through the centre.
Sam Johnstone retains his place in goal ahead of Viljami Sinisalo after making his debut on Wednesday, Cameron Carter-Vickers is back in the heart of defence after missing out entirely in midweek and Kieran Tierney has also recovered from injury
Celtic XI: Johnstone; Donovan, Carter-Vickers, Scales, Tierney; McGregor, Baur Nygren; Duran, Hogh, Tounekti.
Rangers team news
Right, team news news has dropped. First up, here's Rangers, with Derek McInnes selecting his first Old Firm line-up.
The XI is more or less as expected, although Kevin Kelsy is preferred to Findlay Curtis out wide and Dan Neil captains the side from defensive midfield, with Cammy Devlin only on the bench. Ryan Naderi leads the line
Rangers XI: Pandur; Sterling, Fernandez, Makhanya, Penrice; Raskin, Neil; Kim, Gassama, Kelsy; Naderi
Olwethu Makhanya eager to experience Old Firm
Rangers defender Olwethu Makhanya, who signed from Philadelphia Union this summer has said he is relishing the opportunity to play in his first Old Firm.
The South African said: "I think everyone understands what this fixture means to the club, to the fans and everyone. I am really excited and looking forward to it.
"There has been a lot of talking about the fixture, about the history of the derby, but I don't really look into all that. I just know that it is going to be a very passionate game, and I am just excited to be part of it.
"Of course we just have to try and do our job and deliver because we know the fans are going to be behind us, so we are going to use them as an encouragement.
"Also understand that we are also doing it for them; they are going to be very helpful for us."
Martin O'Neill reveals 'timely reminder' given to Celtic by police
Ahead of this afternoon's clash, manager Martin O'Neill says Celtic had a visit from Police Scotland on Friday to give them "a timely reminder" about their "general behaviour" during the clash.
"We had the police come in today, just a little 15-minute meeting to remind us of our behaviour, which I think is a timely reminder," O'Neill revealed.
"They didn't mention this, but I would have assumed that one of the things that would be considered is what happens in the field of play, because these things can be taken further.
"You don't want any sort of punch-ups for a start. Secondly, you don't want excessive celebrations, stuff like that. But I think it's just the behaviour in the light of what has happened in recent fixtures. I think that the conversation with the police wouldn't have taken place had not recent events been brought up to us."
Why are away fans banned this afternoon?
Celtic and Rangers fans have been banned from attending away matches between the Old Firm clubs in the Scottish Premiership and Scottish League Cup this season, which includes this afternoon's Scottish League Cup quarter-final at Ibrox.
The "temporary arrangement" follows the disruption at the Scottish Cup quarter-final between the teams at Ibrox last season, which has led to behind-closed-doors punishments for both clubs in their next home fixture in that competition.
An independent review into the Scottish Cup match at Ibrox found that that "crushing" and "life-threatening violence" were narrowly avoided after Rangers fans stormed the pitch to confront Celtic supporters who had spilled onto the field in celebration.
Read a full explainer on the ban"
Early Celtic team news
Celtic's record signing Kasper Hogh made his return from injury in the 1-0 win at St Johnstone, while Kieran Tierney is nearing a return and could be back in time for the Old Firm.
Martin O'Neill made several changes in midweek, including handing a debut to goalkeeper Sam Johnstone over Viljami Sinisalo, while Cameron Carter-Vickers is expected to be available after being left out entirely on Wednesday
Celtic XI: Johnstone; Donovan, Carter-Vickers, Trusty, Tierney, McGregor, Baur, Nygren, Duran, Hogh, Yang
Early Rangers team news
Rangers captain Lawrence Shankland has been ruled out for months because of a hamstring tear. It's a further blow for Rangers with striker Youssef Chermiti already out with a hamstring injury.
New signing Daisuke Yokota is also out with a hamstring issue while left back Tuur Rommens is getting closer to a return but won't be available yet.
Rangers XI: Pandur; Sterling, Fernandez, Makhanya, Penrice; Raskin, Devlin; Curtis, Kim, Gassama; Naderi
new_text:
Skipper Dan Neil grabbed a glorious double as Derek McInnes claimed his first Old Firm victory as Rangers boss with an emphatic 3-0 Scottish League Cup win over Celtic.
With no away fans inside Ibrox at the order of the authorities amid a ticket allocation spat between the two Glasgow giants, the whole stadium exploded in blue in the 22nd minute when midfielder Neil, signed from Sunderland in the summer, guided in his first Gers goal from the edge of the box.
New striker Kevin Kelsy fired in a second in the 59th minute, his first in Light Blue, with Neil adding a third with another fine finish in the 75th minute as the hosts marched into the semi-finals.
It was a first domestic defeat of the season for Martin O'Neill's side, who rarely threatened the Gers goal - although they will not have long to wait for revenge as the two sides meet in the Scottish Premiership next Sunday where again visiting fans are banned, although after five wins in a row for Rangers, they will travel with confidence.
Follow live updates from Rangers v Celtic, below
Sublime Rangers lay down early Old Firm marker with League Cup hammering of Celtic
Skipper Dan Neil grabbed a glorious double as Derek McInnes claimed his first Old Firm victory as Rangers boss with an emphatic 3-0 Scottish League Cup win over Celtic.
With no away fans inside Ibrox at the order of the authorities amid a ticket allocation spat between the two Glasgow giants, the whole stadium exploded in blue in the 22nd minute when midfielder Neil, signed from Sunderland in the summer, guided in his first Gers goal from the edge of the box.
New striker Kevin Kelsy fired in a second in the 59th minute, his first in Light Blue, with Neil adding a third with another fine finish in the 75th minute as the hosts marched into the semi-finals.
Read the full report from Ibrox:
WATCH: Dan Neil with stunning second to wrap up big win
Dan Neil's first was good but his second was even better. 3-0 and job done
WATCH: Kelsy's exquisite finish makes it 2-0
A lovely volley from Kevin Kelsy to make it 2-0
WATCH: Dan Neil puts Gers in front
Let's have a quick run through the goals from today. Starting with Dan Neil's first strike
Derek McInnes with dream Old Firm debut
It's not been the smoothest start to life as Rangers boss for Derek McInnes (*cough* Jagiellonia Bialystok *cough*) but this will massively help.
One Old Firm derby, one victory for the ex-Hearts man. It was a tactical masterclass as well. His decision to go with three at the back and overload the midfield afforded Rangers complete control.
How will Martin O'Neill respond in seen days' time?
Just seven days until the next Old Firm
Today was great. Fancy doing it again? Of course you do!
Luckily there's only seven day to wait for the next Old Firm clash, with Celtic and Rangers going head to head in the Scottish Premiership next Sunday.
This time, the game is at Celtic Park and there won't be any Gers fans in attendance due to the ongoing ban.
Can Celtic bounce back or will Rangers use this victory to kick on in the league?
Rangers find out semi-final opponents
The semi-final draw for the Scottish League Cup has just been completed, so we now know that Rangers will play Aberdeen at Hampden Park for a place in the final.
That means it's an Edinburgh derby in the other semi as Hearts square off with Hibernian. That's a couple of fun ties.
Scottish League Cup semi-final draw
- Hearts v Hibernian
- Rangers v Aberdeen
Ties to be played on weekend of 31 October / 1 November
Dan Neil: 'We were ready to run through brick walls'
A captain's performance from Dan Neil today and he spoke to Premier Sports after his two goals.
"Brilliant," said Neil. "It was a great team performance. We fully deserved the victory out there.
"I don't score many goals. I thought the big man [Kevin Kelsy] was excellent today.
"In the last few games we've done well without the ball. Today we wanted to use the crowd and get after them - the lads executed it perfectly.
"We all believed in the plan. The gaffer is good before games and he made sure we were ready to run through brick walls. That togetherness and cohesion has really come on recently."
Rangers win first Old Firm of the season
